question: Should OpenClaw permit `gateway.auth.mode: "none"` on non-loopback/private-ingress Gateway binds, and what explicit guardrail or acknowledgement is required if it does?
rationale: The request would move protection for reachable Gateway operator surfaces from OpenClaw auth to external network controls, which is a product/security boundary choice rather than a mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Keep fail-closed by default
options.body: Preserve the current token/password/trusted-proxy requirement for reachable Gateway binds and direct trusted-network deployments to the supported delegated-auth path.

options.title: Sponsor private-ingress opt-in
options.body: Allow no-auth reachable binds only behind a deliberately named high-risk policy with startup warnings, audit findings, documentation, and focused tests.

options.title: Close as not planned
options.body: Reject this trust model in core and close the request after documenting supported token/password and trusted-proxy alternatives.

recommendation.title: Keep fail-closed by default
recommendation.body: Preserve the current token/password/trusted-proxy requirement for reachable Gateway binds and direct trusted-network deployments to the supported delegated-auth path.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent exposed-startup hardening commit and related timeline mentions make this the best available routing owner for the Gateway auth boundary choice.
